item.title: CRAFT: The Prompt Engineering Framework That Every Tech-Professional Needs
item.content:encoded:
The CRAFT Framework for Effective Prompt Engineering Most people, including tech professionals, often use AI sub-optimally due to poor communication and vague problem descriptions. To address this, the CRAFT Framework provides a memorable and effective structure for creating high-quality AI prompts, delivering consistent results across contexts and domains.
CRAFT Framework Overview C - Context & Role: Define the AI's persona and the situation in detail (e.g., expertise, industry, goals, constraints). R - Request & Reason: Clearly specify the task and its goal, starting with an action verb. A - Augment: Guide the AI with examples and chain-of-thought reasoning to improve accuracy and reduce errors. F - Format & Fences: Set the structure for the output and define boundaries for data. T - Trust Boundaries: Include constraints, negative instructions, and guardrails to ensure reliable and safe outputs.

item.title: How AI Quietly Changed Modern UX Patterns
item.content:encoded: Software interaction changed more in the last two years than in the decade before — and most people didn't notice. The article maps the UX patterns that quietly took over: input became intentional (slash commands, selection-based actions, contextual suggestions instead of blank prompts); output became editable instead of regenerate-and-replace; AI moved to where work already happens (Copilot in code, Figma on canvas, Notion in docs); errors turned into conversations rather than dead ends; voice finally became operational; agents started navigating UIs on behalf of users; autonomy turned into a progression (human in/on/over/out of the loop); interfaces became generative and on-demand; and context emerged as the primary design material. The underlying shift: software is moving from task-driven to intent-driven, and design work is moving from static flows to systems that interpret intent, expose the right controls, and maintain trust under increasing autonomy.

The position changes ever so slightly, and so does the exact angle. My phone has changed over the years, from a Samsung S10 to an S21, and now I’m using an iPhone 14 Pro. Alignment is the process of warping each photo so it looks like it was taken from exactly the same angle as a reference image.
